questions.question: Define a trade union and explain why workers join one. Name two South African trade union federations.
questions.expected_answer: A trade union is an organisation of employees formed to protect and promote its members' interests, such as wages, working conditions and job security, mainly by negotiating with employers. Workers join because acting collectively gives them bargaining power that an individual worker does not have. Federations: any two of COSATU, FEDUSA, NACTU, SAFTU.

questions.question: A union representing workers earning R8 000 a month demands 9 percent; the employer offers 5 percent; they settle at 7 percent. Calculate the demand, the offer, the settlement and the new wage.
questions.expected_answer: Demand: 8 000 × 9 ÷ 100 = R720. Offer: 8 000 × 5 ÷ 100 = R400. Settlement: 8 000 × 7 ÷ 100 = R560. New wage: 8 000 + 560 = R8 560 a month (R6 720 more a year).

questions.question: Describe the steps required for a protected strike under the Labour Relations Act, and state one consequence for workers during a protected strike.
questions.expected_answer: The dispute must be referred to the CCMA or a bargaining council for conciliation; a certificate of non-resolution must be issued or 30 days must pass; the union must give at least 48 hours' written notice (7 days if the employer is the state). Workers cannot be dismissed for taking part, but the employer need not pay them for the time on strike (no work, no pay).
